chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Is intercourse disliked during a specific time among the times, even if it is permissible?' He said, 'Yes. Between the emergence of dawn and the emergence of the sun, and from the setting of the sun to the disappearance of the redness (shafaq), and on the day in which the sun is eclipsed, and on the night in which the moon is eclipsed, and on the night and the day in which there is the black wind, the red wind, and the yellow wind, and the day and the night in which there is an earthquake.'

And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) spent the night with one of his wives during a night in which the moon was eclipsed. So there did not occur from him during that night what usually occurred from him during other nights, until he morninged. So she said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah! Is it due to hatred from you during this night?' He said, 'No, but this sign appeared during this night, so I disliked that I should delight and be engrossed therein. And Allah has rebuked a people, so the Mighty and Majestic said in His Book: "If they see a fragment of the sky falling, they will say: Piled up clouds." So leave them until they meet their day on which they will be thunderstruck.'

Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'And I swear by Allah, whoever has intercourse during these times which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade, and the news has reached him, will be granted a child, but he will see in that child what he does not like.'

key_terms.آية: Sign or verse (contextually referring to a divine sign/event)
key_terms.الشفق: The redness in the sky after sunset or before sunrise
key_terms.الكسوف: Eclipse (specifically of the sun or moon)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific times when sexual intercourse is considered disliked in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir) delineates specific times of 'krah' (dislikability) for marital intimacy, linking them to cosmic phenomena like eclipses and earthquakes, which serve as divine signs. The narration highlights the Prophet’s voluntary abstention during a lunar eclipse to avoid distraction from contemplation, illustrating a balance between permissible acts and spiritual mindfulness. This tradition underscores the Shia scholarly view that such timings are not strictly forbidden but are discouraged to preserve the sanctity of the act and potentially influence the character of offspring.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Salim, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is the copulation disliked during a particular time from the timings, and even if it was Permissible?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, whatever is between the emergence of the dawn up to the emergence of the sun, and from the disappearing of the sun up to the disappearance of the redness, and during the day in which is the eclipse of the sun, and during the night in which the moon is eclipsed, and during the night and the day in which there is the black wind and the red wind, and the yellow wind, and the night and the day in which is the earthquake.

And Rasool-Allahsaww had spent the night in the presence of one of hissaww wives during a night in which the moon was eclipsed. So there did not happen to be from himsaww during that night which used to happen from himsaww during others until the morning. So she said to himsaww, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! Is it due to hatred from yousaww during this night?’ Hesaww said: ‘No, but this sign appeared during this night, so Isaww disliked that Isaww should delve in pleasure and the desire therein, and Allahazwj has Rebuked people, so the Mighty and Majestic Said in Hisazwj Book [52:44] And if they should see a portion of the sky coming down, they would say: Piled up clouds [43:83] So leave them plunging into false discourses and sporting until they meet their day which they would thunderbolted with’.

Then Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And I<sup>asws</sup> swear by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, no one would copulate during these timing which Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> has forbidden from, and the news having ended up to him, so he would be Graced with a child, and he would see in that child what he does not like’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘ Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim from his father who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about going to bed with one’s wife; if it is detestable anytime even though it is lawful.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is detestable between dawn and sunrise, from sunset to the disappearance of brightness in the west, on the day of sun eclipse, in the night of moon eclipse, in the day and night of black, red, and yellow winds and in the day and night of an earthquake.

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, passed the night in which a moon eclipse took place with a certain one of his wives and he did not do in that night what he did in other nights until the morning and she asked, “Were you disappointed last night?” He (the Messenger of Allah) replied, “No, but this phenomenon took place last night and I did not like to seek pleasure or amuse myself when Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has reproached certain people in His book, ‘When they see darkness in the sky falling they say, “It is a thick piece of cloud.” Leave them alone until they face their day in which they will be thunderstruck.’ [52:44]’”

Abu Ja‘far, Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘By Allah, whoever after reading this Hadith goes to bed with his wife in such times that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has prohibited and he then is granted a child, will find with the child what he does not like.’”
